title: Lean cross-check of the A5 branch-aware conditional-composition contract
question: Can the already published A5 T6 branch-aware conditional-composition contract be independently checked in Lean and exact Python lanes without changing the existing forward/inverse methods, owner order, claim tier or promotion boundary?
decision_reason: The A5 theorem package already has an operator-confirmed T6 contract, but its exact branch identity and numeric non-identification firewall had no Lean sidecar. R-475 adds only that missing verification layer and does not invent a source owner or re-run a blocked physical-empty/BCC route.
method: Read the canonical A5 conditional-composition manifest and freeze its theorem-contract digest, seven hypotheses, two disjoint branch arrays and top-level weakness map.
Re-derive the scalar and full shell masses from the canonical A1 source manifests with high-precision Decimal arithmetic and require the declared separation threshold.

Compile the R475 Lean entrypoint against the pinned Lean 4.32.1 toolchain; the formal statements are limited to conjunction identity, branch separation, rational mass-fork inequalities and method preservation.
Run a primary exact contract lane, a non-importing independent lane and a fail-closed hostile suite with ten structural, provenance, numeric and promotion mutations.
Run the integrated verifier in temporary child-output paths and record the result only as T0 claim-nonbearing auxiliary support.
finding: The canonical contract digest df01a1a3606d979307ac0bb8c9de14a4ab2d68fd83d228ed38f9e470eba823fc is reproduced by both Python lanes. Primary passes 13/13, independent 9/9, hostile passes 11/11 with all 10 mutations rejected, integrated passes 36/36, and Lean R475 compiles. The initial hostile baseline placement check was corrected to the source manifest's top-level weakness map and then passed fail-closed.
decision_scope: T0 exact sidecar for A5 T6 contract identity, branch separation and source-derived shell-mass non-identification; no analytic A1--A5 theorem is re-proved and no TECT dynamics or physical observable is instantiated.
evidence_level: T0 exact contract cross-check with independent, hostile, integrated and pinned Lean verification
boundary: R-475 improves provenance and arithmetic assurance for the frozen A5 branch boundary only. It does not supply source-owned production dynamics, a common core/norm, cutoff/volume/lattice uniform bounds, an ordered limit, a physical-sector or observation map, Pre-A/Sector-A closure, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity, continuum or mass gap.
assumptions: The operator-confirmed A5 conditional-composition manifest and its hash-pinned authorities are authoritative inputs.
The existing A1--A4 analytic arguments remain the theorem premises; the sidecar checks only their declared contract wiring.
The two Python lanes are audit reproductions and the Lean rational constants are explicitly test oracles, not fitted physical parameters.
Temporary child outputs do not mutate historical A5 run records.
missing_assumptions: A hash-pinned source-owned TECT production generator or transfer with state, projection, filtration and time-boundary contract.
A common invariant core and norm with source-authorized cutoff-, lattice-, volume-, boundary-, phase- and beta-uniform estimates.
An ordered regulator-removal theorem and a physical-sector/observation correspondence with independent holdout data.
A full derivative Class-II constructive measure and BCC existence/selection.
non_claims: No analytic A1--A5 theorem is re-proved by R-475.
No source-owned dynamics, common-core, uniform-estimate, ordered-limit, physical-vacuum, Pre-A, Sector-A closure, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity, continuum or mass-gap conclusion follows.
Shared geometry and the source-derived mass fork do not identify the scalar and full-production state spaces or measures.
R-475 does not alter T-054 forward ownership, T-059/T-061 observation-first inverse methods or their promotion firewalls.

adversarial_review.check: Could the weakness map be read from the wrong object and reject a valid baseline or omit open rows?
adversarial_review.disposition: DISMISSED: the validator now requires the canonical top-level map; the unmutated baseline and its mutation checks pass.

adversarial_review.check: Could the two theorem branches be silently merged or made parameter-identical?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by exact disjoint arrays, the source digest and the merge-branch hostile mutation.

adversarial_review.check: Could hardcoded mass values mask a source change?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: both Python lanes re-derive Decimal values from pinned manifests; collapsed-fork mutation fails. Lean values are labelled test oracles.

adversarial_review.check: Could a T0 sidecar be promoted to a theorem or physical result?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED by tier/claim-bearing checks, method-preservation flags, explicit scope firewalls and non-claims.

adversarial_review.check: Could Lean compilation be described as proving the analytic composition?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: R475.lean contains only the six listed elementary propositions and no analytic operator/domain construction.

next_action: Keep T-054 at the owner-intake gate and do not repeat finite physical-empty or BCC variants. If a real source-owned production dynamics packet and common-core uniform estimates arrive, instantiate a new mainline ordered-limit result with the same evidence contract.
stop_or_redesign: If the canonical A5 source or any authority hash changes, retain the failed audit and issue a new versioned sidecar.
If any child lane fails, a hostile mutation is accepted or Lean stops compiling, keep the failure JSON and reopen the contract audit before citation.
If a future result needs analytic or physical promotion, it must provide new source-owned inputs and an independent holdout or limit proof rather than extending R-475.
